Ah.bar_b_note: B's timber frame, diagonal brace, plank cap and stone footing read as a built wall, but it is still a lone thin panel with flat beige infill under flat even light, and A is a blank white card, far from Palworld's base-building finish.

Mh.bar_b_note: B's larger wrapped candy and pink flask now read at gameplay distance, but rare_candy is an ambiguous brown pile on a cloth and none of the pickups has grounding shadow or rim light against the uniform green carpet.

Vx.bar_b_note: B adds a visible bench with rack and tool shapes beside the tent in the third view, but the station is still tiny at frame scale and the flat, shadowless pale-sand lighting lacks Valheim-class atmosphere.

Ua.bar_b_note: A clear, appealing elder villager with readable eyes, strong white-hair silhouette and an olive/brown palette that fits the meadows family, at a stylised character finish comparable to Palworld's NPCs.

Uf.bar_b_note: Neither side reads as an arch: A is a dark block with cyan studs and B is a narrow blue totem, both standing on a hard-edged square slab dropped onto the moss, so the landmark sinks despite the purple storm sky.

Gp.bar_b_note: B's larger green, blue and gold tiers (gold with a ring) separate better, but they are still similar blobs that read mainly through glow colour, and A's tiers are pinpoint glows on the dark path.

Ja.bar_b_note: A's blue-violet storm wolf holds its fur material and a readable rear-up hit and grounded faint, but B's faint frames turn into a flat white-and-black patched mesh that breaks the creature's identity, and B's hit react is indistinguishable from standing.

En.bar_b_note: B's crisp black-and-yellow banding and hood give a stronger standing silhouette than A's muddy mottled coils, but B's faint mid and end float upright in the air with a detached shadow and wash to pale yellow, and neither side's hit react reads.

Rv.bar_b_note: A's first view shows a curbed bed with a darker filled interior and wooden trim, but in B it is an empty pale stone ring with sand inside that vanishes into the dunes, and neither shows a bedding shape at gameplay distance.

top_changes.change: Replace the placeholder hero props with authored meshes that read by silhouette: a true Crown Arch (two pillars and a spanning crown, seated into the moss with no square slab), a creature bed with a raised straw/cushion nest, and a camp workbench with vice, tools and a work surface

Fix creature hurt/faint states so they keep the base material and stay grounded: no swap to white patched texture (Ja B faint) and no upright floating coils (En B faint), with a distinct hit-react pose

Give pickups gameplay-scale size, contact shadows and tier-coded silhouette plus colour (wrapper shape, base ring, rim light) so Good/Great/Rare candy and meadow items separate at normal camera distance
